fieldsRead.text: TU/e Psychology & Technology studies how people think, behave and interact with technology, combining behavioural science and research with engineering. The displayed Living specialization applies this to healthy, sustainable environments and buildings.

TU/e combines psychology and behavioural research with a 30 EC technical specialization and a required final project. The displayed Living route includes physics, spatial modeling, building circularity and services, healthy environments and lighting. UCR offers related psychological, cognitive, empirical, design and technological methods, but does not reproduce that building-engineering and environmental-psychology sequence, the full human-factors curriculum or compulsory final project.
Living specialization; ordinary 10 EC final project

Ordinary 10 EC final project over the third and fourth quarters of year 3. Entry requires 120 EC, including all compulsory first-year courses, and a pass in either Behavioural Research Methods II or Advanced Research Methods and Research Ethics. The optional 15 EC Innovation Space format is not added to this pathway.

15 EC of open study in year 2, followed by 30 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC of the combined 45 EC must be at intermediate or advanced level, including 15 EC at advanced level. Content must not overlap. Submit a complete study plan for approval after earning 90 EC.
30 EC of open study. Changes to the approved study plan require approval.

Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. Five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities with a combined value of seven add no credits. Personal and professional development is embedded in the core courses.

TU/e requires an ordinary 10 EC final project. UCR optional independent research carries 15 EC and remains outside the scheduled 180 EC.
Perception, cognitive experiments and user-needs product design provide related human-focused methods, but no single selected course establishes the full dedicated Human Factors component.
AI ethics, psychological evidence and algorithmic methods contribute across the programmes; rational-agent planning alone does not establish a full human-centred AI course.
UCR includes actual empirical and statistical projects, but no single selected course is the dedicated technology-related quantitative project. Mathematical sampling algorithms are not that project.
UCR meta-analysis, experimental methods and ethical work provide advanced research contributions, but no single selected course establishes the full advanced-methods and research-ethics unit.
UCR introductory mechanics and physical models support foundations; they do not establish the full physics-for-engineers component.
Consumer-product models and prototypes do not establish a 3D spatial-modeling studio.
Introductory material and environmental concepts do not establish building circularity and energy-performance engineering.
Social, health and sustainability perspectives relate to human needs, but no selected course establishes the dedicated healthy/sustainable living-environment component.
No included course establishes building-services engineering.
Neurobiology includes biological rhythms and sleep and is already shown once; the selected courses do not establish environmental-lighting measurement and design.

A related programme joining psychological and cognitive mechanisms, behavioural research and evidence synthesis with programming, data, intelligent systems, consumer-needs design and introductory physical foundations. Actual psychological experiments, a product-development project and computational work support investigation of people and technology. It differs from TU/e’s dedicated human-factors, environmental-psychology, building-services and spatial-design formation in the Living specialization.

A related programme examining how people adopt, resist and are affected by technology through psychological and qualitative research, product and customer-needs investigation, communication, organizations, digital strategy and AI ethics. Technical data/programming methods support this inquiry. It differs from the dedicated spatial/building engineering and environmental-psychology formation of the comparator’s Living specialization. Introductory physical and material investigation supports the shared consumer-product design work.
